world.title: Football World
world.description: Browse the generated football world: competitions, clubs, players, fixtures and match reports — every row labelled synthetic, with the seed and method that produced it.
world.lede: One locally generated football world — clubs, squads, fixtures, statistics and reports. Public, browsable, and honest about being invented.
world.contentsEyebrow: What is actually in the tables

world.metaMatches: Every fixture in the generated football world, newest first. Scheduled matches show a kick-off time and no score, because no score exists yet.
world.metaNews: Match reports, previews, spotlights and tactical notes from the generated football world. Each one declares whether it is a fact, an analysis or speculation.
world.metaPlayers: Every generated footballer: position, age, overall and potential, plus the season totals that the per-match statistic lines add up to.
world.metaTeams: Every club in the generated football world: city, stadium, manager, formation, squad size and mean overall rating.
world.metaTraining: The generated world's training log: every session names the player, the catalogue drill, the minutes and the RPE, and the load figure is those last two multiplied.

tactics.metaDescription: Fifty authored tactical systems — ten shapes times five temperaments — with the width, spacing and space behind the back line measured from their own coordinates, in metres.
tactics.unavailableDetail: The catalogue is stored on boot by apps/api; start it with scripts/dev.sh.
tactics.eyebrow: Authored coaching structures · measured in metres
tactics.lede: Ten shapes × five temperaments = the fifty systems this lab stores. Nothing here is a real team's play: the coordinates are written by this project, and every figure is measured from them.
tactics.metricsTitle: Every figure on this site, and its formula
tactics.metricsNote: These are the in-possession numbers of one row — {name}. Each system's page prints all eight for both phases, and a measure is never printed without the rule that produced it.
tactics.metricsUnavailable: The metrics table needs at least one stored system.
tactics.emptyNote: The catalogue holds {count} rows; the filter is what is empty.
tactics.boardNote: Each card above prints three of its measured numbers; opening a system draws both phases, lists all eight measures with their formulas, and offers the six counterfactuals. The press line sits at {press_line} m and the defending block is {block_depth} m deep — those two authored values are what the out-of-possession board is derived from.
tactics.boardCompareNote: This one is {formation} under {temperament}. Compare the same shape under a different temperament to see the trade: the same eleven players, measured both ways.
tactics.counterfactualNote: Every change is applied to the stored coordinates and the eight measures are recomputed from the result — the answer is never a conclusion kept in a column.
tactics.unknownChange: “{change}” is not one of the {count} changes this lab offers.
tactics.boardBeforeAfterCaption: hollow = before · dashed arrow = the displacement asked for
tactics.appliesTo: Applies to: {targets} · phase: {phase} · {moved} of {total} measures moved.
tactics.clampedNotice: {count, plural, one {# position} other {# positions}} would have left the pitch, so it was clamped to the touchline or goal line rather than moved the full distance. The table below reports where each player actually ended up.
tactics.bothBoardsNote: Both boards carry the same eleven roles. The defending side is not a second drawing: it is the possession board mapped onto a {block_depth} m block whose top edge is the {press_line} m press line.
tactics.isoEyebrow: §13's third view — the same metres, projected
tactics.isoSummary: Show the isometric projection of the in-possession board
tactics.isoNote: Every dot above went through that pair of lines, from the same x/y metres the in-possession board uses — the projection is arithmetic over the board's own numbers, not a second set of coordinates kept in step by hand. Each marker carries the metres it was projected from beside the point it landed on, so the two can be compared without a screenshot. The lawn, the centre circle and the penalty arcs are the 2D frame's own Law 1 measurements, sampled in metres and projected point by point — a circle on the grass is an ellipse here, and computing that ellipse separately would be a second piece of maths to keep in step with the first.
tactics.isoNotNote: What this is not: a rendered scene. There is no camera, no depth buffer and no lighting, so nothing here can show you what a player would see — it is the plan view bent into a diamond, which is what makes it checkable.
tactics.verdictTitle: What this shape is for, and what it costs
tactics.analysisChipTitle: No AI provider key is configured: the text below is assembled from stored passages, not generated.
tactics.analysisEyebrow: {grounded} statements with a passage behind them · {refused} refused
tactics.analysisTitle: What this lab will say about the shape
tactics.refusedEyebrow: Topics this build refused to answer
tactics.refusedNote: The library has no passage that supports these, and retrieval said so. The alternative was a sentence with a source it did not have, which is the one thing this surface is not for.
tactics.demandsEyebrow: The highest demand in the field for each
tactics.demandsTitle: What it asks of a player
tactics.demandsChipTitle: Compared with your player's own tactical attributes on My Football.
tactics.demandsNote: Six tactical attributes, taken as the maximum demanded by any role this shape fields. They are the same six stored on a player, so fit is a comparison rather than an opinion — the page for your own player shows the pairing.
tactics.siblingsNote: Eleven other systems share this shape; each comparison prints all eight measures side by side, with the formula for every one.
tactics.compareMetaDescription: The same eight measurements, computed for two systems from the same phase, side by side.
tactics.compareUnavailableDetail: The comparison reads the stored catalogue; start the API with scripts/dev.sh.
tactics.compareLede: Two authored structures, the eight measurements, and the difference between them. Nothing is averaged across the pair: each side is computed from its own coordinates.
tactics.compareEmptyNote: {count} systems are loaded for the dropdowns. Until both are chosen nothing is computed — an empty comparison would have to invent a row to show you.
tactics.unknownNotice: “{a}” or “{b}” is not a stored system, so nothing was measured. Pick from the list above.
tactics.noindexNote: Both dropdowns are plain HTML with a GET form, so this page is reachable and shareable without JavaScript; it is noindex because a comparison is a question, not a document.
tactics.boardsMetaDescription: Boards you have arranged in the Tactical Lab, with the measurements recomputed from their coordinates.
tactics.boardsLede: A board starts as a copy of one of the 50 authored systems and becomes yours the moment you move a dot. Its measurements are recomputed by the server from the positions you saved, never from the ones still on screen.
tactics.boardsEmptyNote: Pick a system above and copy it — nothing in the catalogue changes when you do.
tactics.boardsPrivacyChip: only you can read these; a share link is per board and revocable
tactics.editMetaDescription: Drag the eleven players, save the arrangement, and share a read-only link.
tactics.editNoNote: No note yet — this board only exists as positions and the measurements taken from them.
tactics.copiedFromNote: Copied from <link>{system}</link>. That system is unchanged: this is a separate row with your coordinates and `data_origin: user`.
tactics.sharedMetaDescription: A board arranged by a FOOTBALL OS account, with the eight measurements recomputed from its saved positions.
tactics.sharedNoNote: The account that arranged this board left no note with it.
tactics.sharedPanelTitle: Both phases as the owner saved them
tactics.sharedOwnerNote: This page cannot be edited, and the account behind it is named only as “{name}”. <link>Browse the 50 authored systems</link> — those are this project's own, with the reasoning written out on each page.
tactics.sharedRevocableChip: shared by link, revocable by the owner at any time

challenges.title: Manager live challenges
challenges.description: Six authored scenarios — a round window the engine enforces, goals you cannot move, and a verdict summed from the run's own fixtures.
challenges.runsPrivateSuffix: · your runs are private to this account
challenges.lede: A scenario picks the club, fixes the goal and closes the window; the engine plays the rounds. market.lede: A market, not a shop: the board is picked from the band this club is weakest in, every price is the valuation formula recomputed from a stored player row, and the balance is the sum of this career's own move rows. Nothing here was observed; every figure is printed with the expression that made it.

The board picks the best-rated players in the band this club is short in — the need is measured from the engine's own band indices, not chosen by an adjective — and prices each one with the expression printed at the foot of this page.

market.sellingCaption: Selling from {club}: the world stores {stored} players for this club. As of round {round}, {signed} of the players this career fields were brought in by its own moves and {departed} the world stored here are gone. These are the squad's counts, not the ledger's: a signing that is later sold again leaves no trace on either number, while both of its fees stay in this career's ledger.
market.fieldingReads: This squad reads {players} players and {keepers} goalkeeper{plural}. {rule}
market.openPriced: Round {round} priced: {listed} offers on the shelf.
market.openNone: The market answered with no offers.
market.negotiateAnswered: The seller has answered; the price beside the player is the one on file now.
market.loanArrived: {name} arrives on loan until round {round} for {amount} {units}. {effect}

video.metaDescription: Upload a clip, sample its frames, and read what the demo vision provider measured from its pixels.
video.lede: Upload a clip and the pipeline will read its container, sample frames at an even interval, and report where the non-pitch pixels moved. Every detection says which provider made it, and the provider says what it cannot see.
video.emptyNote: Nothing is analysed, and nothing is claimed, until a file arrives.
video.chipOriginTitle: Uploaded by you; never shown to anyone else.
video.privacyChip: the clips are yours; the detections are a demo provider's pixel statistics
video.acceptedNote: Accepted: mp4, MOV and webm, checked from the file's own bytes — a renamed file of another kind is refused, not renamed back. Up to {max} per clip, {limit} clips per account ({used} used). Nothing is published: only this account can read a clip, its frames or its report.
video.ceilingNote: This account holds {limit} clips, which is the ceiling. Delete one to add another.
video.errNoId: The server accepted the file but returned no clip id.
video.errSend: The upload could not be sent: {cause}
video.reportMetaDescription: Frames sampled from an uploaded clip, and the pixel statistics a demo vision provider measured from them.
video.chipOriginTitleReport: Uploaded by this account; never published.
video.chipShaTitle: SHA-256 of the stored bytes, so you can check the file is the one you uploaded.
video.streamNote: Served only to this account, and never advertised to a crawler. {size} bytes, {kbps} kbit/s.
video.cannotPlay: This browser cannot play the file.
video.notAnalysed: No analysis stored for this clip yet.
video.notAnalysedNote: Uploading alone does not measure anything — the pipeline runs when you ask it to.
video.toolsNote: Analysis runs in this request and records a job row for itself; there is no queue and no worker, and the page says so rather than showing a progress bar that nothing is feeding.
video.errComplete: The request could not be completed: {cause}
video.linkedNote: Linking a clip to your football identity or an M6 match lets the clip appear in those contexts and enables richer reports. Both links are optional and can be changed later.
video.shareNote: A share link is a revocable token (§17 pattern). It opens a public read of this clip with no session required and no owner identity disclosed. Revoking clears the token; the clip stays private.
video.framesEyebrow: The frames the measurements came from
video.framesNote: These are the same samples the provider read, converted to PNG for display only. Positions above are fractions of the frame width and height, so they line up with what you see here. Each ring marks one detection's (x, y) on the sample its timestamp falls on — the centre of the non-pitch pixels that provider measured, not a player or a ball — and hovering it prints the timestamp, the confidence and the sentence the measurement was called with.
video.reportProvenanceChip: the clip is yours; the detections are a demo provider's measurements of it
video.sharedMetaDescription: The record a FOOTBALL OS upload leaves behind, handed over by a revocable link — no account required.
video.sharedLede: This link was handed out by an account that uploaded a clip, and the account can revoke it at any time. It discloses the record the upload left behind; the footage itself is served to its owner.
video.chipSharedTitle: Shared via a revocable link; the owner can revoke it at any time.
video.sharedNote: The clip's bytes, its sampled frames and its detection timeline are served to the account that uploaded them, so a shared reader sees what the upload recorded rather than the footage. Playing a clip needs the owner's session.
video.sharedProvenanceChip: shared via revocable link; no owner identity is disclosed here

myFootball.metaDescription: Your player profile, attribute progress and today's coach recommendation.

portfolio.metaDescription: The ten sections of your football CV, each read from the rows that already exist, and the two this build cannot fill.

gallery.metaDescription: Tactical boards arranged by FOOTBALL OS accounts who chose to show them — each one measured from the dots its owner placed.
gallery.lede: Every board here stands because its owner pressed the button that lists it, and leaves the moment they withdraw. What is shown is the drawing, its measurements and the owner's display name — nothing else about the account.
gallery.emptyNote: No account has listed a board yet. Arrange one in the Tactical Lab and press List publicly to stand here.
gallery.sampleNote: The measurements above are recomputed from the stored dots on every read — the same arithmetic the owner's own page serves, never a snapshot.
gallery.consentChip: each board stands by its owner's revocable consent
gallery.boardMetaDescription: {name} — a tactical board in the public gallery, measured from the dots its owner placed.
gallery.boardLede: One board from the public gallery: the owner's own arrangement, with every measurement recomputed from the dots they placed.
gallery.boardTitle: The board, as its owner left it
gallery.noteNote: This is a user's drawing, not the project's coaching work. The fifty authored systems are
gallery.catalogueLink: in the Tactical Lab, with their reasoning written out

community.metaDescription: What your account publishes, the feed that reaches you, and the rules that decide who reads a post.
community.headLede: A post here is a pointer and the author's own words: it names the page it shares and stores no figure about it, so what you read beside a share is counted from the rows the moment you ask. Reach is a predicate over follows, recomputed on every read — unfollowing someone withdraws their posts at once and deletes nothing.
community.composerEyebrow: {following} of {followingMax} followed · {posts} posts and {follows} follow rows on the platform
community.feedEyebrow: {total} reachable · {printed} printed · a feed of {authors} author(s)
community.feedNote: The follow button on a row is decided from the authors this feed lists, because the tier publishes counts and no list of who follows whom. A followed account with nothing reachable here is not shown as followed.
community.refusalsEyebrow: {count} codes · one status each, from the project’s one table
community.refusalsTitle: What a door here refuses, and with what answer
community.refusalsNote: There is no 403 in this tier: a community door asks only whether you have a session, and what you may not reach is answered as absence — the same shape a row that was never written earns, so no door confirms that somebody else's private wall exists.
community.pointersEyebrow: {count} kinds that point, and the page each one names
community.pointersTitle: Where a pointer has to land
community.pointersNote: A `note` points at nothing and every other kind must point under its own prefix; the door refuses the pair otherwise, with the prefix it expected in the refusal.
community.limitsEyebrowOne: one limit, stated by the API on every read
community.limitsTitle: What this tier does not do
community.limitsNote: Nothing here is gated on a plan: the entitlement table has no community feature today, so publishing costs nothing and the ceilings above are row counts, not prices. Read the vocabulary at /api/v1/community/rules, which needs no account.
community.profileUnreadable: Your own wall counts could not be read, so this page has nothing to size the ceilings against.
community.kindLabel: Kind — a note carries words, everything else carries the address of your own artifact
community.visibilityLabel: Visibility — reach is decided by the follow rows, not by a list stored on the post
community.wordsLabel: Words (at most {max} characters, and never blank)
community.pointerLabel: Points at {prefix} plus the artifact address — this kind names the {kind} page, and the tier stores the address, never a figure read from it
community.ceiling: This account holds the {max} posts the tier allows, so the door is closed until one is erased.
community.repliesEmpty: no reply has been written on this post
community.replyCeiling: This post holds the {max} comments the tier allows; the door will refuse a further one and say so.
community.pointerBroken: pointer is not under its kind prefix
community.pointerNone: points at nothing — a note is words only
community.totalAgrees: the door total is the number of rows it printed
community.pointersAgree: every row pointer sits under its own kind prefix
community.pointersMismatch: {n} row(s) whose pointer is not under its kind prefix
community.emptyWall: Nothing reaches you yet. Follow an account, or publish the first post — {posts} of {max} used.

simulate.metaDescription: Play a fixture between two generated clubs from their stored squads and an authored tactical system.
simulate.worldNotReady: The simulator plays from stored squads, and the generated world is not present in full yet.
simulate.headEyebrow: {name} · simulations are private to this account
simulate.headLede: Every figure below is a model output, printed with the rate that produced it. The scoreline is what this model did with these two squads — not what a real match would have produced.
simulate.modelTitle: What the model claims about itself
simulate.scorelineNote: A scoreline from here is a description of what this model does with these inputs. It is not a forecast, and the clubs are not real. <link>The knowledge library</link> explains what the numbers mean in football terms; it does not vouch for any single match.
simulate.reportNoList: the report arrived without a list
simulate.listError: The list could not be read: {detail}
simulate.emptyBody: Pick two clubs above and the report will appear here once it has been stored.
simulate.provenanceExtra: stored rows keep the seed, so a match can be re-derived and its digest compared
simulate.seedError: A seed has to be a whole number between 0 and 2,147,483,647 — or blank, so the server picks one and stores it.
simulate.noPathError: The server played the match but returned no link to its report.
simulate.swapTitle: Play the tie the other way round
simulate.seedPlaceholder: blank: the server picks and stores one
simulate.formNote: A tactical system adds the metres the Tactical Lab measured from its eleven coordinates; without one the match is played from the club's own formation and those inputs stay empty. The seed is kept with the match, so the same fixture and seed replay to the same report — {calibration}
simulate.seedTitle: The seed that replays this row exactly
simulate.reportDescription: A block-by-block report from the possession-block model, with the inputs, formulas and seed that produced it.
simulate.noReport: The stored row came back without its report, so nothing on this page is rendered from memory.
simulate.digestTitle: SHA-256 prefix of the report, taken before the digest key existed.
simulate.totalsEyebrow: {home} v {away} · as the engine counted them
simulate.totalsNote: Goals in the model: {goals} of {shots} shots, against {xg} expected goals. A model that scores fewer goals than its own xG is not broken — the xG is a sum of probabilities and each chance was rolled once.
simulate.tracedTitle: An event names a player only when that side's eleven holds the name once.
simulate.ambiguousNames: {count, plural, one {name} other {names}} on this timeline belong to two players in the same eleven ({names}), so those events are kept without a player rather than guessed at.
simulate.unnamedNames: {count, plural, one {event} other {events}} named the club rather than a player ({names}), which is what the engine prints when a side has no eleven to name from.
simulate.blocksEyebrow: {count} blocks · the model rolls inside a block, not minute by minute
simulate.blocksNote: Each multiplier is printed exactly as the model applied it, including the ones that did nothing: a<mono> man_down_attack </mono>of 1.00 means nobody was sent off in that block, and a<mono> fatigue </mono>below 1.00 is the model reducing shot volume as the match runs on.
simulate.inputsEyebrow: Measured from stored rows, not chosen for the page
simulate.ownerNote: Only this account can read a stored match. Nothing here is a forecast: <lab>the Tactical Lab</lab> is where the shapes come from, and <lib>the knowledge library</lib> is where the terms mean something.
simulate.inputsFromTitle: The tables the inputs were read from
simulate.mHighTurnoversWon: Turnovers won in the final third
simulate.timelineEmpty: The model produced no goal-bound event, card or injury in this match. An empty timeline is a result, not a missing fetch — the totals above add up to it.
simulate.multiplierLine: vol {volume} · quality {quality} · fatigue {fatigue} · late space {lateSpace} · stretch {stretch} · opponent open {opponentOpen} · man-down {manAttack}/{manConcede}
simulate.noTactics: No tactical system was chosen for this side, so the shape metrics are empty: the match was played from the club's own formation and nothing was measured from a pitch shape.
simulate.notModelEyebrow: What this model does not model
simulate.replayUnable: The check could not run: {reason}. The stored digest stays what it was — nothing here pretends to have re-derived it.
simulate.clubGone: one of the clubs is no longer in the generated world
simulate.replayIdentical: Identical. Playing the same two squads, systems, length and seed through {version} produced {replayed} again, which is the digest on this row.
simulate.replayNotIdentical: Not identical. The row says {stored} and a fresh run says {replayed}. The engine moved without its version moving, so this match is no longer reproducible and is kept as a record of what was claimed.

club.titleLimits: What this tier does not do

club.eyebrowEntitlements: {plan} plan · {ceilings} ceiling(s) for this tenant · as of {asOf}

home.metaTitle: Watch. Understand. Train. Play. Manage. Become.
home.metaDescription: FOOTBALL OS is a football operating system for fans, players and coaches. Today the AI player-coach vertical slice works end to end; the live football-world modules are still being built.
home.heroLede: One system for the whole football journey — follow the game, learn it, train against an explainable AI coach, and watch a player profile grow from real sessions.
home.moduleLiveBody: Live scores are not shown because no match feed is licensed yet. This module ships with M3 Football World.
home.moduleWorldBodyOn: Football World ships with M3 (module status: {status}). No fixtures, tables or transfers are displayed because no data source is connected.
home.moduleWorldBodyOff: Football World ships with M3. No fixtures or transfers are shown — the capabilities endpoint is currently unreachable.
home.moduleNewsBody: No news headlines are rendered because no provider is licensed. When it lands, every item will carry its source.
home.notBuiltHint: This module is on the roadmap and not implemented yet.
home.signInTitle: Sign in to see your football
home.signInBody: Your OVR, streak and completed sessions appear here once you have an account and a player profile.
home.noPlayerBody: Create your football identity to start earning XP and growing attributes.
home.whatWorksLede: The M1 player & AI-coach vertical slice runs end to end. Everything below uses real requests against the backend — nothing here is faked.
home.featureTrainingBody: A library of drills with setup, instructions, coaching points, common mistakes and progressions.
home.featureCoachBody: Ask for a recommendation and get the chosen drill plus the reasons behind it — every answer is labelled demo vs live.
home.featureProgressBody: Completing sessions awards XP and nudges the attributes a drill targets, so your OVR is earned, not invented.
home.featureDataBody: Export your sessions and attributes, or delete everything you have stored, straight from settings.
home.policySyntheticBody: Player profiles, attributes and content in this build are synthetic demo data. They are not real athletes and are labelled as demo wherever they appear.
home.policyLicensedBody: No club, league, player imagery or broadcast assets are used or claimed. Anything that would need a licence simply is not shown yet.

careerDetail.metaDescription: One career's rounds, the record summed from them, and the objectives it is judged against.
careerDetail.lede: Every number below is summed from the rounds this career has played, and each one prints the formula it used. The results come from the labelled simulation engine — no fixture here reports a real match.
careerDetail.nextUp: Next up: round {round}, {venue} {opponent}{at}. {rotation} The seed for the round is {seed}, which is derived from the career and the round number before the engine is asked anything.
careerDetail.recordEyebrow: summed from the rounds listed below
careerDetail.challengeNotice: This season is a challenge run: the objective, the philosophy and the budget came from the scenario {slug}, and its window of {window} rounds is enforced when a round is played.
careerDetail.noObjective: No objective is stored on this career, so nothing below can be called success.
careerDetail.noRoundBody: Press “Play the next round” above: the engine will pick the eleven from stored squads and keep every number it used.
careerDetail.carryTitle: What the played rounds left on the players
careerDetail.rowLoadWindow: Window the load is measured over
careerDetail.rowMeanCondition: Mean condition of the last round's eleven
careerDetail.noLoadBody: This career’s next side will be measured off its club’s stored rows, at the form the world wrote — {formula}
careerDetail.tableTitle: Table of the clubs this career has met
careerDetail.engineTitle: What the engine was told, and what it was not
careerDetail.clubGone: the club is no longer in the generated world
careerDetail.ledgerTitle: Who did it, counted off the event rows
careerDetail.rowGoalsAttemptsXg: Goals / attempts / xG for the club
careerDetail.rowEventsWithoutPlayer: Events with no player behind the name
careerDetail.everyEventAttributed: none: every event the club printed found exactly one player
careerDetail.ledgerEmptyNoRows: None of this career’s rounds has event rows on file, so there is nothing to group. Play a round and the rows arrive with its report.
